audits.title: Implementing evidence based medicine in general practice: audit and qualitative study of antithrombotic treatment for atrial fibrillation.
audits.standard: Evidence-based antithrombotic (warfarin) treatment for patients with atrial fibrillation at risk of thromboembolism
audits.setting: General practice, Tonbridge, south east England

cycle1.result: 132 of 13 239 patients had a history of atrial fibrillation, 100 of them at risk of thromboembolism.

audits.intervention: Assessment and educational interview with eligible patients about antithrombotic treatment.

cycle2.result: After the study 52 patients were taking warfarin; of the other 48 (41 on aspirin), eight too ill, 16 unable to consent, four refused interview and 20 declined warfarin.

audits.other_findings: Patients' unwillingness to take warfarin was a major limiting factor; those declining sought a higher level of benefit.
audits.citation: Howitt A, Armstrong D. Implementing evidence based medicine in general practice: audit and qualitative study of antithrombotic treatment for atrial fibrillation. BMJ. 1999;318(7194):1324-1327. doi:10.1136/bmj.318.7194.1324. PMID: 10323820.

audits.title: The Disconnect Between Novel Oral Anticoagulant Eligibility and Provincial Drug Coverage: An Albertan Anticoagulation Clinic Audit.
audits.standard: Canadian guidelines recommending NOAC in preference to warfarin in nonvalvular AF
audits.setting: Single-centre anticoagulation clinic, University of Alberta, Edmonton

cycle1.result: 89%-95% eligible for NOAC but only 39%-41% qualified for provincial drug coverage

audits.other_findings: Gap between guideline-recommended therapy and drug coverage.
audits.citation: Dhillon SK, McMurtry MS, Bungard TJ. The Disconnect Between Novel Oral Anticoagulant Eligibility and Provincial Drug Coverage: An Albertan Anticoagulation Clinic Audit. Can J Cardiol. 2015;31(8):1047-1050. doi:10.1016/j.cjca.2015.02.027. PMID: 26095931.

audits.title: Adherence to antithrombotic therapy guidelines and atrial fibrillation in a rural hospital: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Antithrombotic guidelines according to CHADS2 and CHA2DS2-VASc scores
audits.setting: Rural country hospital, South Australia; retrospective inpatient cohort

cycle1.result: 77% received appropriate anticoagulation according to CHADS2 score and 83% according to CHA2DS2-VASc score.

audits.citation: Aziz H, Mills D, Newbury J. Adherence to antithrombotic therapy guidelines and atrial fibrillation in a rural hospital: a clinical audit. Rural Remote Health. 2019;19(1):4342. doi:10.22605/rrh4342. PMID: 30889960.

audits.title: Reasons for omitting anticoagulant treatment in patients with atrial fibrillation: an audit of patient records in general practice.
audits.standard: Recommendation for anticoagulant treatment in most patients with atrial fibrillation

cycle1.result: Absence of anticoagulation based on an explicit clinical decision in 93.4%; unjustified or outdated decisions in 6.6%.

audits.other_findings: 59.0% had no follow-up plan; decision documented at least once for 94.6%, revised in the past year for 22.3%.
audits.citation: Laugesen IG, Mygind A, Grove EL, Bro F. Reasons for omitting anticoagulant treatment in patients with atrial fibrillation: an audit of patient records in general practice. BMC Prim Care. 2025;26(1):166. doi:10.1186/s12875-025-02852-8. PMID: 40375165.

audits.title: A clinical audit of oral anticoagulant therapy in aged care residents with atrial fibrillation.
audits.standard: Australian guideline recommendations for anticoagulation in non-valvular atrial fibrillation
audits.setting: Nineteen aged care facilities in southeast Queensland

cycle1.result: Of 356 residents with non-valvular AF at high stroke risk, 172 (48.3%) were prescribed an oral anticoagulant and 40 (11.2%) had a documented decision not to prescribe; dose consistent with recommendations in 44.8%.

audits.other_findings: 1754 residents screened, 359 (20.4%) with non-valvular AF; 76.8% of anticoagulated residents received non-vitamin K antagonists.
audits.citation: Bernaitis N, Bowden M, La Caze A. A clinical audit of oral anticoagulant therapy in aged care residents with atrial fibrillation. Int J Clin Pharm. 2020;42(2):474-481. doi:10.1007/s11096-020-01025-0. PMID: 32291550.
